Game Models
Positional Play · Relacionismo · Pressing · Set Pieces
Two core philosophies: Positional Play for structured build-up and ball control; Relacionismo for fluid combination play through relational links. Both share the same cognitive foundation — players who think faster than the game.
Positional Play
4-3-3 morphing into 3-2-2-3. Third-man runs, staircase combinations (escadinhas). Creates positional and numerical superiorities — including deliberate 1v1 situations for wingers to exploit in the final third.
Relacionismo
The Brazilian relational model — build-up through relationships and combinations. Fluid roles, wall passes (tabela), escadinhas and dummy runs. Proximity and timing over rigid positional instruction.
Pressing System
High block with 4-player press unit. Clear triggers. Gegenpressing within 6 seconds of ball loss. Channel to flank, compress and trap.
Set Pieces
Designed corner routines with blocking screens, timed runs and 2v1 overloads in the box. Two variants with specific player roles and counter-press organised on every delivery.
Cognitive First
Players solve the problem before touching the ball — scanning, anticipation and pre-decisions trained daily
Positional Superiority
Create numerical and positional advantages in every zone — including deliberate isolation of wingers in 1v1
Emotional Aggression
Players perform under stress, recover from mistakes, and lead with competitive emotional drive
Context Adaptability
Model adapts to opponent, squad profile and game phase — core principles never lost

03
Relacionismo
Relational Build-Up · Escadinhas · Tabela · Dummy Runs
Relacionismo is the Brazilian relational model — build-up constructed through player relationships and combination play. Fluid links, wall passes, escadinhas and intelligent dummy runs create unpredictability that structured defences cannot solve.
What are Escadinhas?
Escadinhas (literally "staircases") describe diagonal positioning that allows progression through quick relational links. Each player plays, moves diagonally, and becomes available at a higher line — creating a staircase pattern that breaks defensive lines without long balls or individual dribbles.
Relacionismo — relational combination play
Speed:
Escadinhas + Dummy Run
Escadinhas & Dummy — relational progression
Speed:
Proximity Over Position
Combinations emerge from spatial proximity — players react to who is closest
Tabela (Wall Pass)
Two-touch combinations through defenders — the tabela as a core movement pattern
Escadinhas Rhythm
Play → diagonal move → receive higher — staircase links that progress the ball
Dummy Runs
Intelligent runs without the ball — pulling defenders, creating space for the actual receiver
Fluid Roles
No fixed positions in build-up — players interchange based on flow and proximity
Cognitive Anticipation
Players read partner movements before the ball arrives — relational play demands faster thinking
04
Pressing
High Block · 4-Player Unit · 6-Second Rule
High pressing system led by a coordinated 4-player unit. Clear triggers, cover shadows and flank traps. On ball loss, gegenpressing within 6 seconds before reorganising into the compact block.
High Block — 4-player press unit
Speed:
4-Player Unit
Two strikers + two advanced midfielders press as one — never solo chasing
Cover Shadow
Unit cuts passing lanes before closing — shadow the ball, force backward or wide
GK Trigger
Ball to GK → unit activates immediately — close CBs, cut central pass option
Touchline Trap
Force wide → compress FB + winger — touchline orientation, 2v1 trap
6-Second Counter-Press
Ball lost → nearest 3 press within 6 seconds — deny build-up before opponent organises
Rest-Defense Structure
Gegenpress fails → sprint into compact block — rest-defense shape protected at all times
Press Triggers
GK receives

CB under pressure
Back pass to GK
Flank overload achieved

Training Exercises
Cognitive Load · Fun · Pressing · Transition
Every exercise maps directly to a game situation. Sessions build cognitive load progressively across all five training dimensions.
Exercise 1 — Pressing Rondo
Pressing · Cognitive
Pressing Rondo — 7 touches then switch quadrant
Speed:
Setup: Two adjacent zones. Possession team targets 7 consecutive passes — after 7 touches they switch to the next zone. If the pressing team wins the ball, they shoot on goal immediately.

Focus: Pressing shape, cover shadows, triggers, decision-making under cognitive load.
Exercise 2 — Pressing Rondo (Mini-Game)
Pressing · High intensity
Pressing Rondo — mini-game variation
Speed:
Setup: Tighter-space rondo variation. Pressing team can shoot immediately on winning the ball.

Focus: Individual pressing technique, body orientation, anticipation before pressing.
Exercise 3 — Cycle to 4v4
Transition · SSP
Cycle to 4v4 — GK distributes, teams cycle attack/defend
Speed:
Setup: Small-sided pitch, two goals. GK at centre distributes to one team — they attack immediately while the other defends. After goal or ball out, GK plays to the other team and roles switch instantly. Continuous cycle.

Focus: Positive and negative transition speed, defensive shape recovery, attacking intent under time pressure.
Exercise 4 — Fun 2v2 Mini-Game
Fun · Speed
Setup: Fast 2v2 — the moment a goal is scored or ball goes out, the next pair enters immediately. High tempo, continuous, competitive.

Focus: Quick combinations, 1v1 duels, pressing in pairs, decision-making at speed. Joy and competitive drive are part of the design.
